hourly.summary: Manchester United fans are in full-blown meltdown mode after the team dropped into the relegation zone following a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. Michael Carrick is being absolutely savaged for his tactics, selections (especially Dalot), and post-match platitudes, with supporters demanding his immediate sacking. The Pochettino debate rages as a desperate Plan B, but the overarching mood is pure toxicity — fans screaming at executives, players telling each other to 'look at themselves', and a club that feels completely rudderless.

daily.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remained in a state of unrelenting crisis throughout the day, with all four snapshots registering a dire 2/10 as the team sat 18th in the table after a chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. The mood never wavered from full-blown panic — fans demanded the immediate removal of Michael Carrick, the hierarchy, and the ownership, while gallows humor about relegation and planned protests underscored a fanbase that has completely lost faith. No improvement or shift in tone appeared across the timeline; the Theatre of Dreams remained firmly the Theatre of Nightmares from dawn to dusk.

weekly.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remained locked in a cataclysmic 2/10 crisis throughout the week, briefly punctuated only by a fleeting false dawn on October 28th when Kobbie Mainoo's return temporarily lifted spirits to 7/10 before injury setbacks and dressing-room fractures crashed the mood back to rock bottom. The dominant arc is one of deepening structural resignation: a nine-game winless streak, genuine relegation fears, unified fury at the Glazers and INEOS, and a pervasive belief that the squad has downed tools have calcified the fanbase into radioactive gallows humor and total abandonment of hope.
